ADR-RUN-0020.statement: The sc-storage crate MUST expose the shared asynchronous Storage<T> contract without dependencies outside the Rust standard library.
SQLite, Postgres and MySQL MUST implement the same Storage<T> contract.
Storage<T> MUST provide read, read_all and write operations for application-defined row types.
StorageRow MUST describe the row table, key, columns, encoding and decoding through validated row descriptors.
Consumer row types, schemas and migrations MUST remain outside generic engine implementations.
AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) MUST commit or roll back its multiple row operations as one atomic unit.
Generic transaction handles MUST provide read, write, insert and delete operations across row types.
Each transaction retry MUST start a fresh owned Send + 'static producer future.
TransactionSpec MUST expose name and read-only/read-write mode through constructors and accessors with a non-exhaustive public shape.
Engine configuration MUST provide finite retry and deadline defaults.
The transaction contract MUST preserve the option of adding transaction-specific retry policy without breaking consumer construction.
Transaction observations MUST retain name, queue wait, run time, row-operation count and outcome.
Generic engines MUST quote validated identifiers and bind row values instead of accepting consumer SQL strings.
Storage failures MUST return typed StorageError values with stable code, retryability, source and recovery information.
Public storage functions MUST NOT panic.
The SQLite implementation MUST admit writes through a bounded asynchronous channel to one dedicated writer thread owning the sole write-mode connection.
The SQLite writer MUST batch admitted writes and send successful replies only after the outer transaction commits.
SQLite reads MUST use the reader workers of the same database implementation.
Only the dedicated SQLite writer thread MAY drive Runtime::block_on; reader workers MUST receive with blocking_recv without a runtime.
Async storage callers MUST NOT block or wrap storage submission in spawn_blocking.
A SQLite write transaction body that yields MUST roll back with a typed error.
SQLite writer failure MUST fail all admitted replies and close further admission.
CronStore<S> MUST keep its generic backend private behind the policy-checked CronStorage facade.
CronStorage MUST enforce active-name admission, configured schedule-row limits, generation fencing and multi-row mutations through atomic domain operations implemented once in sc-cron.
SQLite application and cron rows MUST share the application database by default.
Generation MUST reject cron when no database is selected.
Legacy cron import MUST preserve stored fields through an idempotent, read-only-source migration that refuses collisions atomically.
sc-cron MUST own CronRow and MontyBlobRow tables and migrations through generic row storage.
Schedule writes MUST reject Monty source that sc-monty cannot compile.
sc-cron MUST capture the compiled hook-session blob immediately after compilation and before any hook runs.
sc-cron MUST key each compiled-session blob by sc-sha SHA-256 of the source and the Monty dump version.
sc-cron MUST use a cached blob only when its key matches the authoritative source stored in the schedule row.
A missing, stale, corrupt or unreadable-version blob, or a loaded session missing cron_stop or cron_tick, MUST cause recompilation from source and replacement of the cached pre-run blob.
sc-cron MUST NOT persist hook run state in compiled-session blobs.
Backend factories and open options MUST belong to the corresponding engine implementation.
Application WidgetStorage, OpenWidgetStore and StoresView extensions MUST preserve generated identifiers and existing create, read and delete behavior.
Phase D MUST publish sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands and sc-monty together at version 0.3.0.
Phase D MUST retain table-neutral Postgres and MySQL engine implementations in the generated template rather than introduce additional published engine crates.

ADR-RUN-0021.statement: CLI, MCP and HTTP interfaces MUST invoke the same application command read and write paths through the daemon.
The daemon command path MUST be reachable over HTTP through a Unix-domain socket or TCP transport.
sc-command MUST provide asynchronous storage_read(store, transform, key) and storage_write(store, transform, input) functions over Storage<T>.
Command failures MUST return typed StorageCommandError values.
A command with directly convertible Tcli and Tsql types MUST use built-in conversion and storage behavior without requiring an application-written transform or storage action.
Application business rules MUST enter the shared path through the open Transform seam.
Cron command storage MUST use the sc-cron-commands policy adapter to CronStorage without exposing its raw backend or duplicating cron policy.
Documentation MUST identify Transform, storage_read and storage_write as provisional in version 0.3.0.

The command seam MUST permit later addition of a second transform input, a typed Ok outcome that writes nothing distinct from Err, and a transform within an atomic transaction without breaking consumers.
Those three deferred command-seam behaviors are outside Phase D implementation scope; this does not prohibit later addition.
The Phase D interpreter transform MUST complete before the storage transaction begins.
Monty compilation, sessions, resource limits, host-function dispatch, typed interpreter errors and session dump/load MUST be implemented only in sc-monty.
sc-monty MUST expose a compiled session and value-level MontyInvoke<Tin,Tout> invocation of a script and named function with typed inputs and output.
At d-5 closure, sc-monty normal and build dependencies MUST be limited to pydantic Monty crates, excluding sc-*, Tokio and serde_json.
At d-5 closure, sc-monty source and tests MUST NOT define cron types, cron-reserved names or a copied scheduler/store implementation.
Interpreter extraction MUST begin with an exact copy of the current sc-cron code, dependencies and unit/integration tests that passes before any API change.
The passing baseline commit MUST remain reachable from the d-5 closing commit.
Interpreter separation MUST preserve every copied assertion.
sc-cron MUST call sc-monty for interpreter execution while retaining its own cron policy and JSON/value conversion.
Monty cron hooks MUST receive values rather than JSON strings.
Monty command transforms MUST call sc-monty directly with source read at invocation from an application-owned UTF-8 file configured at daemon setup.
Transform source replacement MUST take effect without rebuilding the application.
Transform source file-read and UTF-8 errors MUST return typed transform failures.
The bounded interpreter execution adapter MUST keep blocking interpreter work off Tokio request workers.
The interpreter execution adapter MUST NOT block storage submission.
Generated applications MUST be able to select Monty without selecting cron.
The template widget create and delete commands MUST use storage_write.
The template widget get command MUST use storage_read.
cron.start and cron.end MUST use storage_write.
cron.list MUST use storage_read.
The Phase D user commands cron.start, cron.end and cron.list MUST use the shared command path.
cron.start MUST allow the configured application transform to modify or append user JSON before schedule persistence.
Command-path requirements MUST NOT mandate hand-written code or prohibit a later consumer-side generator against the delivered framework.
